title: The Algorithm at the End of Humanity?
author: B
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Former Google DeepMind researcher Bilal Chughtai has joined a group of artificial intelligence specialists warning that capable systems could pose an existential threat to humanity.

Chughtai, who worked on artificial general intelligence safety and alignment, left Google DeepMind in July 2026. In a statement, he said he believed AI could kill everyone and warned that society might be running out of time to prevent an outcome. Google did not comment on his remarks.

His intervention followed the resignation of Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who said concern about catastrophic AI risks partly motivated his departure. Anthropic scientist Evan Hubinger supported Coxon’s warning and estimated that the probability of AI causing humanity’s extinction within the next decade was greater than 10%.

These claims are forecasts from individual researchers, not established predictions. Nevertheless, they have intensified debate over whether the commercial race to build more powerful AI is moving faster than efforts to understand and control the technology.

Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei has called for slowing the development of advanced systems. His proposal received unusual support from industry figures, including SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk and OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman. The appeal has also renewed arguments about “AI doomerism,” a label often applied to concerns about worst-case outcomes.

Chughtai maintained that AI could be developed safely, but said success would require coordination among rival companies. He argued that development should proceed at a pace society can manage, allowing emerging dangers to be identified before they produce extreme harm.

Political agreement remains elusive. President Donald Trump dismissed the industry’s push for regulation as a hoax, highlighting the divide between advocates of stronger safeguards and those concerned that restrictions could impede innovation. The dispute leaves governments facing a question: how to respond to uncertain but potentially irreversible risks without overstating what current evidence can prove.

Reuters — “Ex-Google DeepMind researcher adds to warnings that AI could ‘kill all humans’”, September 15, 2026.
Channel NewsAsia — Reuters report republished, September 15, 2026.
